questions.stem: Ms. Okafor ___ the quarterly report every Friday afternoon.

why_wrong: B : Passif : Ms. Okafor fait l'action.
D : Le prétérit ne convient pas à une habitude présente (« every Friday »).
B: Passive: Ms. Okafor does the action.
D: The past tense does not fit a present habit ('every Friday').

questions.stem: The factory ___ at full capacity since the new machines were installed in March.

fr.rule: Since + point de départ passé → present perfect.
why_wrong: B : « since » demande un temps de l'accomplissement.
C : Le progressif passé ne marque pas le lien avec le présent.

en.rule: Since + past starting point → present perfect.
why_wrong: C: The past progressive does not link to the present.

questions.stem: When the auditors ___ next week, all records should be ready.

fr.rule: Subordonnée de temps : présent à valeur future.
why_wrong: A : Present perfect : pas de lien avec « next week ».
C : Prétérit : le sens est futur.
D : Pas de « will » dans une subordonnée de temps.

en.rule: Time clause: present with future meaning.
why_wrong: A: Present perfect: not consistent with 'next week'.
C: Past tense: the meaning is future.
D: No 'will' in a time clause.

questions.stem: By the end of this year, the company ___ its headquarters to a larger building.

why_wrong: A : Le présent ne marque pas l'achèvement avant « by the end of ».
B : Present perfect : incompatible avec « by the end of this year » (futur).
C : Prétérit : le sens est futur.
fr.example: By May, I will have finished.

why_wrong: A: The present does not show completion before 'by the end of'.
B: Present perfect: inconsistent with future 'by the end of this year'.
C: Past tense: the meaning is future.
en.example: By May, I will have finished.

questions.stem: Our accounting department ___ a new software program at the moment.

why_wrong: A : Present perfect : pas de lien avec « at the moment ».
B : Prétérit : « at the moment » demande le présent continu.
D : Le présent simple décrit une habitude, pas « at the moment ».
A: Present perfect: not consistent with 'at the moment'.
B: Past tense: 'at the moment' needs the present progressive.
D: The simple present describes a habit, not 'at the moment'.

questions.stem: The list of attendees ___ available at the registration desk.

fr.rule: Accord avec le noyau du sujet.
why_wrong: A : Pluriel : le sujet est singulier.
D : Le sujet est « list » (singulier), pas « attendees ».
fr.example: The key to success is effort.

en.rule: Agree with the head noun of the subject.
why_wrong: A: Plural: the subject is singular.
en.example: The key to success is effort.

questions.stem: Each of the technicians ___ responsible for a separate section of the plant.

why_wrong: B : Forme de base sans accord.
fr.example: Each of them has a key.

en.example: Each of them has a key.

questions.stem: Neither the director nor the project managers ___ aware of the policy change.

fr.rule: Neither/nor : accord avec le sujet le plus proche.
why_wrong: A : Singulier et présent : le contexte est au passé et le sujet proche est pluriel.
C : Singulier : le sujet proche est pluriel.
D : Accord avec le sujet le plus proche : « managers » (pluriel).
fr.example: Neither he nor they are late.

en.rule: Neither/nor: agree with the nearest subject.
why_wrong: A: Singular present: wrong tense and number.
C: Singular: the nearest subject is plural.
D: Agreement with the nearest subject: 'managers' (plural).
en.example: Neither he nor they are late.

questions.stem: The news about the merger ___ welcomed by shareholders.
All visitors ___ to sign in at the front desk upon arrival.

fr.rule: be required to = être tenu de.
why_wrong: A : Actif : les visiteurs ne « requièrent » pas.
fr.example: Staff are required to wear badges.

why_wrong: D: Present participle with no auxiliary.
en.example: Staff are required to wear badges.

questions.stem: The new safety regulations ___ into effect on January 1.

fr.rule: Certains verbes ne se mettent jamais au passif.
why_wrong: B : « go into effect » est actif.
fr.example: The law goes into effect soon.

en.example: The law goes into effect soon.

questions.stem: The conference room ___ for a client presentation this afternoon.

why_wrong: A : Actif : la salle ne réserve pas.
C : Actif au présent : même problème.

en.rule: The subject receives the action → passive.
why_wrong: A: Active: the room does not reserve.

questions.stem: Please return the signed contract ___ the end of the week.

why_wrong: A : « since » + point de départ passé.
D : « until » indique une durée, pas une échéance.
D: 'until' marks duration, not a deadline.

questions.stem: The training workshop will take place ___ June 14.

why_wrong: A : « in » s'emploie avec un mois ou une année seuls.
B : « at » s'emploie avec une heure.
A: 'in' is used with a month or year alone.
B: 'at' is used with a clock time.

questions.stem: We are very interested ___ expanding our business to Southeast Asia.
___ the heavy rain, the outdoor event proceeded as planned.

why_wrong: A : Cause : le sens est une opposition.
B : Cause : le sens est une opposition.
A: Cause: the meaning is contrast.
B: Cause: the meaning is contrast.
C: Source of information: wrong meaning.

questions.stem: ___ the conference was expensive, many employees still chose to attend.

why_wrong: A : Cause : le sens est une opposition.
B : Préposition : elle ne peut pas introduire une proposition.
A: Cause: the meaning is contrast.
B: Preposition: cannot introduce a clause.

questions.stem: Please arrive early ___ the session can begin on time.

fr.rule: So that + sujet + verbe = pour que.
why_wrong: B : = au cas où : le sens est la précaution, pas le but.
fr.example: Speak slowly so that everyone understands.

en.rule: So that + subject + verb = in order that.
why_wrong: B: = just in case: precaution, not purpose.
en.example: Speak slowly so that everyone understands.

questions.stem: Employees may work from home ___ they complete their tasks on time.

fr.rule: As long as = à condition que.
why_wrong: C : = au cas où : sens différent.
fr.example: You can go as long as you're quiet.

why_wrong: C: = just in case: different meaning.
en.example: You can go as long as you're quiet.

questions.stem: The candidate ___ resume impressed the committee was offered the job.

why_wrong: A : Cas régime, pas de possession.
fr.example: The man whose car was stolen called.

en.example: The man whose car was stolen called.

questions.stem: The conference, ___ takes place every year in Chicago, attracts thousands of visitors.

fr.rule: Relative non restrictive : which, pas that.
why_wrong: A : « that » ne s'emploie pas après une virgule.
C : Pas un pronom relatif ici.
fr.example: The report, which is long, is ready.

why_wrong: A: 'that' is not used after a comma.
C: Not a relative pronoun here.
en.example: The report, which is long, is ready.

questions.stem: Ms. Duval will present the findings ___.

why_wrong: D : Pronom objet simple, pas d'emphase.
D: Plain object pronoun, no emphasis.

questions.stem: Mr. Chen is looking for ___ apartment close to his office.

why_wrong: B : Appartement non précisé : pas de défini.
C : « apartment » commence par un son voyelle.
B: Unspecified apartment: no definite article.
C: 'apartment' starts with a vowel sound.

questions.stem: This year's profits were ___ than last year's.

why_wrong: A : Superlatif : « than » demande un comparatif.

questions.stem: Employees ___ submit their expense reports within 30 days; it is company policy.

why_wrong: B : Conditionnel : ne convient pas à une règle.
C : Possibilité faible : une règle demande une obligation.
D : Capacité ou possibilité : pas d'obligation.
B: Conditional: does not suit a rule.
C: Weak possibility: a rule requires obligation.
D: Ability or possibility: no obligation.

questions.stem: ___ we received your payment earlier, the order would have shipped on time.

fr.rule: Had + sujet + p.p. = if … had + p.p.
why_wrong: A : « If we received » : mauvais temps ; irréel passé exigerait « had received ».
fr.example: Had I known, I would have called.

en.rule: Had + subject + p.p. = if … had + p.p.
why_wrong: A: 'If we received' is the wrong tense for the unreal past.
en.example: Had I known, I would have called.

questions.stem: The board has decided ___ the company's headquarters next year.

why_wrong: D : Forme de base : « to » manque.

questions.stem: The ___ employees were rewarded with an extra day off.

why_wrong: D : Adverbe : un adjectif est attendu devant un nom.
D: Adverb: an adjective is expected before a noun.

questions.stem: The ___ of the new software has reduced processing time by half.

why_wrong: C : Verbe : nom attendu après « the ».
D : Adjectif : un nom est attendu après « the ».
D: Adjective: a noun is expected after 'the'.

questions.stem: Please review the ___ document before the meeting.

en.rule: Past participle used as an adjective.

A: 'that' does not fit a question.
